angle: geography and registries: EPA ECHO NAICS 336611 by state, shipbuildinghistory.com active-yard registry, river-by-river and coast-by-coast searches, Navy distributed-shipbuilding partner lists, welder postings
notes: Independent list built without opening ledger/plants.csv, evidence.csv, links.csv, inbox or any audit file about this vertical; an `ls` of ledger/audit showed file names (incl. fact-check/list-audit A for this vertical) but no contents were read. Method: (1) EPA ECHO get_facilities NAICS 336611 national pull (1,393 rows; 1,030 active) used as a state-by-state candidate registry; it is dominated by on-base repair contractors, coaters, marinas and closed yards, so each candidate was checked against a live page. (2) shipbuildinghistory.com / navalmarinearchive.com active small- and large-yard registry and 2021 barge-delivery table. (3) River/coast sweeps (Ohio, Monongahela, Mississippi upper/lower, Illinois, Tennessee/Cumberland, GIWW Louisiana/Texas, Mobile Bay/Bayou La Batre, Florida, Great Lakes, PNW, California, Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Alaska). (4) Navy distributed-shipbuilding / submarine-industrial-base supplier lists (HII 2025-26 releases, EB/Austal/BAE module work). (5) MARAD Small Shipyard Grant recipient lists FY2024-FY2026 as a small-yard registry. (6) Welder job-posting searches by city (Houma, Mobile/Pascagoula, Ohio River). All quotes were confirmed on the live page with tools/fetch_page.py --check (quote_verified true). Judgement calls: yards doing both repair and some new construction or Navy module work are marked in (e.g., Colonna's, BAE Jacksonville, JT Marine, Southwest Shipyard). Planned/not-yet-operating yards (Anduril Arsenal-2, Saronic Port Alpha) are listed out. Repair-only and aluminum-only rows are a bounded set of near-misses, not an exhaustive list; Navy public yards (Norfolk, Portsmouth, Puget Sound, Pearl Harbor) and the many ECHO-listed on-base repair contractors were not added. Several in-definition rows rest on older sources (Leevac, New Generation, Boconco, Marine Builders, Sneed Orange, Duckworth) and current activity is unconfirmed. WebFetch unused (broken); maritime.dot.gov, USNI, gdbiw.com, gdeb.com and several company sites blocked or failed; trade-press copies used instead. searches_until_dry = 72: search #72 (MARAD FY2026 Small Shipyard Grant list) was the last to add new in-definition plants (LAD Services, Signet, Vessel Repair); the seven later discovery searches (#73, #76, #77, #80, #81, #82, #84 incl. FY2023-FY2025 grant lists, Texas coast, PNW fishing builders, Austal partners) added none; #74-75, #78-79, #83 were verification lookups. Registries are not fully exhausted: unresolved builder-like names from ECHO 336611 and grant lists that were NOT checked or could not be confirmed include Ocean Marine Shipbuilding, Off Shore Trawlers, Bayou Shipbuilding & Services, Raymond & Associates (AL); Superior Shipyard & Fabrication, International Shipyard, Seville Industries, Marine Industrial Fabrication, A&Z Marine, Low Land Construction, Gulf Coast Industries, A&B Industries (LA); Texas Barge & Boat, Burton Shipyard, Lighthouse Marine (TX); Superior Marine Ways (OH), Amherst Industries/Amherst Madison (WV), Campbell Transportation (PA), Three Rivers Boat & Barge (KY), Mike's Inc (IL), Sunflower Enterprises (IA), Western Towboat, Stabbert (WA), Highmark Marine Fabrication (AK), Norseman Shipbuilding (FL), Textron Systems New Orleans (SSC, likely aluminum). ECHO was used for discovery only, not reconciled row-by-row. One row per yard except: Eastern Panama City (Nelson St + Allanton combined) and Bludworth (Galveston/Houston, generic multi-yard source). Gulf Ship (Chouest) and Bollinger Gulfport Shipbuilding are treated as separate Gulfport yards (no acquisition found). Rodriguez has a second Bayou La Batre yard not listed separately.
